subject: Business
title: Inflation: The Silent Thief
description: A quick win: understand Inflation: The Silent Thief.

hook.text: In 1980, a movie ticket cost $2.69. Today it costs $11. Your salary may have grown. Your purchasing power may not have.

buildup.text: Inflation is the general increase in prices over time, reducing the purchasing power of each dollar.

discovery.text: Central banks target about 2% inflation per year. At that rate, prices double every 36 years.

twist.text: Keeping cash under a mattress loses value every year. Savings accounts below the inflation rate also lose value.

climax.text: Venezuela's hyperinflation hit 1,000,000% in 2018. A cup of coffee cost more in the afternoon than the morning.

punchline.text: Money in your pocket is money losing value. Invest it or inflation takes it.

quiz.question: At 2% annual inflation, how long does it take for prices to double?

details.summary: Inflation is the gradual increase in prices that erodes purchasing power over time. At 3 percent annual inflation, prices double roughly every 24 years, meaning money sitting in a savings account is quietly losing real value even as the nominal balance stays the same.
details.whyItMatters: Inflation is the reason saving alone is not enough. Money must be invested to grow faster than inflation, or its purchasing power steadily erodes. Understanding inflation is essential for any long-term financial plan.
takeaways: Inflation reduces what your money can buy even as nominal amounts stay the same
At 3 percent inflation prices double approximately every 24 years
Investments must outpace inflation to preserve real purchasing power

faq.question: How is inflation measured in practice?
faq.answer: The Consumer Price Index tracks the average cost of a basket of typical goods and services over time. When the CPI rises 3 percent in a year, that basket costs 3 percent more. Core CPI excludes volatile food and energy prices for a smoother trend.

faq.question: How can you protect your money against inflation?
faq.answer: Stocks have historically returned 7 to 10 percent annually, well above inflation. Real estate, commodities, and TIPS bonds that adjust for CPI also provide inflation protection. Cash and fixed-rate bonds lose real value when inflation exceeds their returns.
